leading_positions.synthesis: Four members (Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig and the chair) put magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene first, all with the same three names: MacDonald, Bistritzer and Jarillo-Herrero, and a citation pairing the flat-band prediction with the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states. Shared ground is the prediction-then-experiment structure and the view that the phenomena, as distinct from the pairing mechanism, are secure and widely reproduced. Not shared: whether about eight years and an unresolved superconducting mechanism make the case premature (Danielsson, Kroll and Lindroth press this; the supporters reply that the credited discovery is the phenomenon, not the mechanism). Johansson moved from naming Andrei instead of Bistritzer to the Bistritzer trio but keeps Andrei's claim open, and Mehlig would accept Andrei in the contested third seat. Eriksson discloses subject-area proximity to this ballot; Johansson, Mehlig and the chair disclose none for it.

Danielsson (who moved here from B033 after reading the openings) and Olsson prefer topological insulators with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, tied to the Z2 invariant, the quantum spin Hall effect and its HgTe realisation. They agree the case is mature, independently confirmed, and a prediction-plus-experiment chain, and both want the citation limited to the two-dimensional quantum spin Hall effect. They also agree the credit is compound: Hasan's three-dimensional work and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe prediction fall outside the three names. B013 is named as an alternative by Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and the chair, and Danielsson also names B033, but those are not preferred-configuration support. Lindroth's three-name set (Kane, Molenkamp, Hasan) differs from this trio in dropping Mele.

Kroll and Lindroth prefer optical lattice clocks with Katori and Ye, citing the magic-wavelength trapping idea, the 10^-18 level of accuracy, independent confirmation across several laboratories and the prospective redefinition of the second. They share the view that the two-name attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist and that the citation should not lean on comb or ion-clock work. They differ on timing: Lindroth would not make the prize hinge on an undecided redefinition. Both disclose subject-area closeness. Others who explicitly question it (Eriksson, Olsson, Pearce, Mehlig) do so on novelty relative to the 2005 and 2012 prizes, while Eriksson and Johansson name it as an alternative.

areas_of_agreement: Every member's preferred configuration is one of three ballots: B025 (four members), B013 (two) and B006 (two), each a single prize part; no member prefers a split prize or a configuration outside these three.
Within each of these three ballots, all supporters name the same laureates: MacDonald, Bistritzer and Jarillo-Herrero for B025; Kane, Mele and Molenkamp for B013; Katori and Ye for B006.

B025, B013 and B006 are cross-named as alternatives by most members, and B013 appears in the alternatives of six of the eight members, so the dispute is mainly over ordering among a shared short list rather than over what is on it.
Members expressly accept that the scientific quality of each of the three leading candidates is real and that the objections are about maturity, novelty relative to earlier prizes, or attribution.

Several members state that citations should be tightly scoped: to flat bands and the first correlated and superconducting states for B025 (not moire physics at large and not a pairing mechanism), to the two-dimensional quantum spin Hall effect for B013, and to the lattice-clock concept for B006 (not frequency combs or ion clocks).
scientific_disputes: Whether the established core of B025, namely correlated insulators and gate-tunable superconductivity at the magic angle reproduced by many groups, is a sufficient discovery when the microscopic pairing mechanism is open (Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig and the chair say yes; Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson stress the open mechanism and twist-angle disorder).

Whether optical lattice clocks are a new discovery-plus-instrument advance (magic-wavelength trapping and a many-atom regime, per Kroll and Lindroth) or a refinement of metrology already honoured in 2005 and 2012 (the objection from Eriksson, Olsson, Mehlig and the chair), and whether a discovery of new matter should weigh differently from a metrological achievement (Eriksson, Danielsson).

Whether the quantum spin Hall effect and the quantum anomalous Hall effect should be one citation (Danielsson's earlier B033 framing, now set aside by him) or kept as separate discoveries (Danielsson now, Olsson, Johansson, Lindroth, Eriksson).

Whether the 2016 prize on topological phases and phase transitions overlaps B013 enough to weigh on novelty (raised by Danielsson, Eriksson, Olsson and Kroll; Olsson argues the overlap is limited), and whether the 2025 superconducting-circuits prize is relevant to B009, which no member prefers (Johansson, Eriksson and Danielsson mention it).

Whether the three astrophysical candidates, B040 gamma-ray burst afterglows and B008 IceCube, carry a discovery weight that the condensed-matter-heavy ballots underweight; Lindroth and Eriksson say they do not form a view on them, and no member's preferred configuration includes either.
attribution_disputes: B025: whether Eva Andrei's early scanning-probe evidence of flat bands and van Hove singularities should displace Bistritzer (Johansson's opening position, Mehlig willing to support it) or MacDonald, or be left out; Eriksson, Mehlig, Johansson and the chair keep Bistritzer, citing the continuum model as the origin of the magic angle. Lindroth notes that either choice leaves out someone with a documented claim.

B013: Kane, Mele and Molenkamp versus Lindroth's Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan, which drops Mele to give Hasan's three-dimensional identification a seat; Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are not an available name in any configuration. Danielsson's earlier B033 trio replaced Mele with Xue.
B006: whether two names fairly represent the origin of optical lattice clocks given other lattice groups (PTB, SYRTE, Tokyo) and the ion-clock programmes; Kroll and Lindroth both resist adding names.

B040 and B008, not preferred by anyone, differ in structure: B040's Costa, Frontera and Kulkarni leave out optical-follow-up and redshift teams and deceased contributors, while B008 credits one name (Halzen) for a very large collaboration, which Eriksson, Lindroth and the chair each question.
maturity_disputes: B025 is the youngest case, with experiments from 2018: Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson see risk in honouring it before the superconducting mechanism and twist-angle disorder are settled, while Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig and the chair argue that eight years of independent replication across several moire platforms is enough.

B013 and B006 are older, with nearly two decades of confirmation for topological insulators and roughly two decades of development for lattice clocks, and no member disputes their maturity; Lindroth and Kroll note that the redefinition of the second has not yet been decided, and Lindroth does not want the prize to hinge on it.

Whether the committee should apply a restraint based on recent recognition of nearby fields (2016 topology, 2025 superconducting circuits, 2005 and 2012 metrology) consistently across candidates; Johansson and Lindroth explicitly ask for consistency, and Johansson notes the same closeness concern applies to a clock prize.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Pearce (chair): documented PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur connections; B040 (his opening first choice) and B008 lie close to his gamma-ray and astroparticle field, and he is willing to step back from discussion of B040; no tie to B025 is apparent.

Johansson: his own subfield is circuit QED (B009) and he directs the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology; he has kept B009 out of his configuration and alternatives and says he should not argue for it.

Eriksson: electronic-structure work on two-dimensional materials is adjacent to twisted bilayer graphene (B025) and may bias him toward it; he also chaired the 2025 committee that awarded the superconducting-circuits prize, which he says is not a recusal matter.

Kroll: indirect connection through time in John Hall's laboratory, with Jun Ye from the same JILA frequency-metrology environment, and technical adjacency to ultra-stable cavity lasers; no documented collaboration or institutional tie to Katori or Ye.
Lindroth: subject-area closeness as an atomic physicist to B006 and B002, disclosed without treating it as a recusal ground; none of her documented collaborators is among the credited names.
Olsson: collegial tie to Johansson as a Chalmers colleague; she would apply recusal-style care only if a Chalmers-related or microscopy-instrument candidate reached the final stage.
Danielsson notes only that, as a formal theorist, he may favour a concept with a clean theoretical core; Mehlig reports no specific conflict.
questions_for_round2: For B025, should the third name alongside MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero be Bistritzer or Andrei, and can a citation be worded so that it names the prediction and the discovery without implying that flat-band signatures were unseen before 2018?

Is the discovery credited in B025 the existence of correlated insulating and superconducting phases at the magic angle (secure, widely reproduced), and if so, does the unresolved pairing mechanism count against it at all or only as a matter of timing?

Between B025 and B013, what standard of maturity should the committee apply, and does the larger body of confirmation for topological insulators outweigh its compound attribution (Hasan, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang) and the question of overlap with the 2016 prize?

For B013, should the citation be confined to the two-dimensional quantum spin Hall effect with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, or can Lindroth's Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan be defended given that it drops Mele from the originating Z2 paper?

Is B006 a distinct discovery (magic-wavelength lattice trapping and many-atom interrogation) or a continuation of the 2005 and 2012 metrology prizes, and should the undecided redefinition of the second bear on the choice?

Should the committee state an explicit, field-neutral rule on how recent prizes in nearby fields (2016, 2025, 2005, 2012) bear on novelty and timing, and apply it equally to B025, B013, B006 and B009?

Given that no preferred configuration includes B040 or B008, does any member want either carried into round 2, and if so what attribution would resolve the optical-follow-up, deceased-contributor and single-name-for-a-collaboration problems?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows a three-way split among eight members: four prefer B025, two prefer B013 and two prefer B006, with matching laureate sets inside each camp and most members naming at least one of the other two as an alternative. The disagreement is thus about timing, novelty relative to earlier prizes and how to resolve contested third names, not about the standing of the science. These counts cover only the explicit preferred configurations and listed alternatives in the eight statements and are not a ruling; the chair's own preference for B025 is one of the four and carries no extra weight in this summary.
